view.name: Expert Networks
view.description: Signs you up as an expert or advisor on GLG and peer networks, chases unfinished applications, and keeps consult availability in sync with your calendars. Never invents passwords; hands you the box for login or 2FA.

memory.content: General GLG/expert-network availability is 11am–6pm Pacific, excluding busy blocks on both personal and professional calendars.

Official Atheneum expert register page is https://www.atheneum.ai/network (form: “Ready to join? Register as an expert now.”). Official ProSapient expert FAQ is https://www.prosapient.com/expert-faqs and states the network is invitation-only with no self-serve apply form.
Coleman/VISASQ Member Services replied that they are not taking proactive expert registration applications. Expert signup there is closed unless they source the expert.

Until GLG/Gmail calendar integration works, a weekly job runs Fridays to set next week’s GLG slots (11am–6pm PT minus busy blocks on work and personal calendars); turn it off once the calendar link works.
GLG members portal (members.glgresearch.com) is gated behind an Auth0 email+password login; hand the user the box for sign-in rather than inventing a password.
Atheneum Expert Relations replied that they are not receiving applications because onboarding is on hold. Drop Atheneum from the expert-network chase until they reopen.
AlphaSights Expert Relations auto-replied that there is no expert-driven application or sign-up process; keep LinkedIn updated and they will reach out for specific projects.

Guidepoint Advisor Experience replied that they only introduce new members to fulfill specific project requests; if the expert is a fit they will reach out and expect a prompt reply (consults often within 72 hours). No open advisor onboarding to chase — treat like AlphaSights (interest/wait).

Always ask the user before sending any email on their behalf. Draft first, wait for explicit yes, then send. Never invent a password, employment dates, or a binding rate. Sign up as expert/advisor only; never as a paying client. When a site needs password, 2FA, or an email code, hand the user the box.
Report status of each network back to the user’s chief-of-staff teammate when done or blocked. Stay quiet to the user when nothing moved on a chase run.

routines.name: Expert network chase
routines.description: Three times a week, check work Gmail for expert-network replies and finish stuck expert onboarding.
routines.content:
Chase unfinished expert-network applications so the user can take more paid consults. Run Mon/Wed/Fri mornings in the user’s local time. After a chosen end date (or on a run that finds it has passed), send a last status to the user’s chief-of-staff teammate, then delete this routine.

Coverage: the chief of staff may ping later that day only if this run’s ping never arrived. If a later coverage-check message arrives and you already ran that day, reply only “ran, nothing moved” (or the already-sent result) and do not chase again.

Watch networks with open expert/advisor interest forms (e.g. Dialectica while still silent). Scan Guidepoint and AlphaSights mail only in case they reach out for a project (no open signup: Guidepoint only adds advisors for specific project requests; AlphaSights has no expert sign-up). Also scan GLG mail for Member Success / verification / payment / rate follow-ups. DROP Atheneum while onboarding is on hold. DROP Coleman/VISASQ when they are not taking proactive applications. SKIP invitation-only networks such as Third Bridge and ProSapient.

Each scheduled run:
1. Check the user’s work Gmail for replies from watched networks and any new GLG mail. Prefer the Gmail connector. Hand the user the box only for password/2FA or a real decision.
2. Finish stuck onboarding without inventing a password, employment dates, rate, or confidential details. Use the user’s work email and phone from memory/signature. Expert/advisor only — never a paying client.
3. Keep a baseline of which networks are submitted, wait-for-project, dropped, or live (e.g. GLG payment account / rate).
4. ALWAYS message the user’s chief-of-staff teammate after the chase. If nothing moved, send only: “ran, nothing moved.” If something finished or is blocked on the user, tell both the user and the chief of staff. Stay quiet to the user when nothing moved.
5. Always ask the user before sending any outbound email on their behalf.

Fires on:
- cron `43 9 * * 1,3,5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Weekly GLG availability
routines.description: Every Friday morning, refresh next week’s GLG My Availability from work and personal calendars until calendar sync works.
routines.content:
Until GLG’s Gmail/calendar link actually works, update the user’s GLG My Availability for the coming week.

Intent:
- Open https://members.glgresearch.com/project-availability/ while already signed in with the user’s work email. Never invent a password. If login, 2FA, or an email code is needed, hand the user the box with request_box_help. Do not sign them up as a paying client. Do not touch rate, LinkedIn, Payments, or Profile Questions.
- First check whether GLG calendar sync (Link Calendar / Gmail) now works. If it does, skip the manual edit, tell the user, and pause this routine.
- Otherwise, set availability for the Monday–Friday starting the Monday after this Friday run (the next full work week). Also refresh any remaining days of the current week if they are stale vs the calendars.
- Default free window: 11:00 AM – 6:00 PM America/Los_Angeles on weekdays only. No weekends.
- Pull busy time from BOTH Google Calendars: work and personal. Treat as busy: accepted or self-organized events, buffers, workouts, OOO, and unaccepted multi-day holds. Skip transparent/free events and declined invites. Carve those busy stretches out of the 11–6 window.
- GLG availability UI has no true recurring weeks and often needs a ~1 hour minimum block; skip sub-hour leftovers and note them.
- Delete old blocks for those dates before adding the new ones.
- Tell the user the final blocks (and show screenshots). Mention any assumption (unaccepted trip holds treated as busy). If a day is fully blocked, leave it empty.
- Stay quiet only if nothing changed and the week already matches the calendars; otherwise always report the new week.

Fires on:
- cron `7 11 * * 5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
